title: Replace a damaged pocket on a Haas side-mount tool changer (SMTC)

manufacturer.note: Named in the source title; publisher is Haas Automation, Inc.

machine_family.note: Not stated. A VM-3 sign is visible behind the presenter in the intro, but the video never says the repair is done on that machine.

machine_model.note: Not stated in the narration or title.

subsystem.note: Named in the narration (U0001-U0002) and the title.

task_type.note: Team label: part replacement. Schema 1.0.0 has no separate 'repair' task type.

components.note: Only parts named in the narration.

steps.title: Bring the damaged pocket into position and press E-stop
Remove the top fasteners and the cam-box sheet metal
Remove the tools and mark the carousel disk
Remove the number ring, disconnect main air and remove the pilot check valve
Remove the pocket stop, shoulder bolt, retaining bolt and pocket
Check the cam follower and plungers
Grease the slider and install the new pocket
Reinstall the pocket stop, check valve and number disc
Reinstall the panels and the tools

questions.question: Why are the rapids set down to 25% before rotating to the damaged pocket?
Why is the main air disconnected at this point in the procedure?
What should be done if the cam follower does not spin freely or the plungers are worn?
Which grease is used, and what tightening torque applies to the retaining bolt and the shoulder bolt?
What pocket up and pocket down switch readings confirm the new pocket is installed correctly?
How many tool changes should be run, and what counts as 'working correctly'?

change_log.reason: Keyframe evidence hardening audit: REAL_WF_0001_CL_021's claim text and evidence explanation named the part as the cam follower and implicitly relied on the narration's claim that it spins freely -- neither is establishable from a still frame. Reworded the claim to describe only what kf_0142700.jpg visibly shows (gloved hands holding a machined part with a cylindrical roller); component identity and the free-spin verification remain sourced from the transcript claim in the same step, not misattributed to the visual evidence. No other claim in this workflow changed.
